races.title: State Assembly, District 33
races.note: The top two finishers from the Nov 3, 2026 count. Everyone else in this race is coming.

cands.name: Hipolito Angel Cerros
cands.bio: Democratic candidate for California State Assembly District 33. Born and raised in Lindsay, UC Davis graduate, and former Lindsay city councilmember who served as Mayor Pro Tem and then Mayor. Says he is the youngest mayor in California history.

endorsements.text: Listed by Ballotpedia as receiving voter guide recommendations from two Sway voting groups: 'Unburdening The Ballot: Voting Made Easy' and 'Yaysayers'. No organizational or official endorsements were identified.

cands.gaps: We could not find his positions on data centers, homestead property taxes, limits on investor or foreign land buyers, H-1B and immigration enforcement, gun policy, abortion, school choice and teacher pay, or police funding. His campaign site names priorities (water, workforce training, rural healthcare, economic development) but gives no detailed policy statements. We found no documented votes or actions from his time on the Lindsay City Council, and no news coverage of his record or of any controversies. His campaign site gives no dates for his council service, and we could not confirm them. He did not complete Ballotpedia's candidate survey in 2024 or 2026.

local.label: Roots 100: His campaign website says he was born and raised in Lindsay, California, and calls himself a lifelong Central Valley resident.

score.why: Raised $0, under $5,000 for this office: too little money to score fairly.

qual.background: Served four years on the Lindsay City Council, including as Mayor Pro Tem and Mayor, per his campaign site. He interned in the California State Senate and with the U.S. Conference of Mayors, and earned a Harvard edX public policy certificate.
qual.why: Local elected office (city council and mayor) puts him in the middle range. He has no state legislative service and no documented law or budget career. Internships and board seats were not counted.
qual.label: Local elected office (city council and mayor) puts him in the middle range. He has no state legislative service and no documented law or budget career. Internships and board seats were not counted.

slow-growth-protect-land.evidence: His campaign priorities page lists protecting Central Valley agricultural land and preserving water, with investment in water storage and infrastructure. It gives no specific growth-limit or development policy.

prio.label: Matches 1 of 1 priorities; 0 backed by their record, 1 only promised (needs 2 to score)

roots.summary: His campaign website says he was born and raised in Lindsay, California, and calls himself a lifelong Central Valley resident.

cands.name: Alexandra (Ali) Macedo
cands.bio: Republican Assembly member for District 33 since December 2024. Fourth-generation Tulare native, president of Macedo Environmental Consulting, Inc., and a 2021 San Joaquin College of Law graduate. Her family runs a livestock market and farms almonds.

endorsements.text: Republican Party of California (2026 endorsement per Ballotpedia)

cands.gaps: The list of bills she has sponsored did not load, so we could not confirm any specific bill she authored. We found no documented stances or actions from her on data centers, homestead property taxes, limits on investor or foreign land buying, gun laws, abortion, or H-1B visas. Her site says she opposes new taxes and wants fewer rules so more homes can be built, but gives nothing specific on property taxes or growth limits. On immigration she calls for federal border security and an easier legal system for farm labor, which we could not classify. We did not find her bar admission status, exact dates for her business career, or a teacher-pay position. Ballotpedia says she did not complete its candidate survey in 2024 or 2026.

local.label: Roots 100: Ballotpedia lists her birthplace as Tulare, CA, and her campaign biography says she was born and raised in Tulare, attended Tulare Union High School, and returned to the Central Valley after college.

score.why: Raised $0, under $5,000 for this office: too little money to score fairly.

qual.background: Assembly member for District 33 since December 2024. President of an environmental and agricultural consulting firm that works with state and regional regulators. Earned a law degree in 2021 and helps run a family livestock market.
qual.why: She has held legislative office since December 2024 and has a law degree. She has also run a regulatory-compliance consulting business. Her time in the Legislature is relatively short, so she scores at the low end of the high range.
qual.label: She has held legislative office since December 2024 and has a law degree. She has also run a regulatory-compliance consulting business. Her time in the Legislature is relatively short, so she scores at the low end of the high range.

back-police-order.evidence: Says she supports getting rid of pro-criminal laws that reduced penalties for property and violent crimes, so lawbreakers face a price.

school-choice-teachers.evidence: Says she supports making charter schools easier to set up and making sure they have the money they need.
